steps.title: The orbit
steps.say: The Earth travels around the Sun once a year, and its axis is tilted 23.5° and always points the same way.

steps.title: Northern winter
steps.say: In December the north end of the axis leans away from the Sun, so northern sunlight hits at a low angle and spreads out. Days are short and it is winter.

steps.title: Spring
steps.say: A quarter of a year later, neither pole leans toward the Sun. The Sun is over the equator and the north is warming up.

steps.title: Northern summer
steps.say: In June the north leans toward the Sun. Sunlight hits more directly and days are long, so it is summer in the north, and winter in the south.

steps.title: Autumn
steps.say: By September the tilt is sideways to the Sun again. The Sun is over the equator and the north is cooling.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.say: Seasons come from the tilt, not from distance to the Sun. Now drag the Earth to where it is summer in the south.
